bug_semantics: An authenticated low-privilege requester could omit ComponentId, causing FileServer to classify the request as the always-allowed “Personal space,” and supply any non-null TypeUpload plus an absolute SourceFile. The TypeUpload branch treated the attacker-controlled SourceFile as an absolute filesystem path and streamed it, bypassing component authorization and repository-root confinement and exposing arbitrary server-readable files (CWE-36).
flaw_origin: Legacy SVN/CVS-era web-core import: the complete vulnerable request-to-path and null-component authorization logic first entered this Git repository in the 2009 bulk addition of war-core, then survived formatting, package moves, and refactors until the 2026 fix.

Direct fix: https://github.com/Silverpeas/Silverpeas-Core/commit/caa6e6d1ac967ebd29b39e11c2ef5e7fd0047eec (“Fix bug #15229”, 2026-03-20) removes TYPE_UPLOAD_PARAMETER and descriptor.absolutePath(), rejects undefined ComponentId with HTTP 400, separates missing-session redirect from authorization failure, returns HTTP 403 for unauthorized components, and eliminates the componentId == null allow branch. First-party tracker reference is https://tracker.silverpeas.org/issues/15229 (the public endpoint redirects to login).

reasoning: The advisory’s attack condition is not merely a generic traversal: omitting ComponentId selects an authorization special case that returns true, and the independent presence of TypeUpload switches attacker-controlled SourceFile into absolute-path mode. Following both decisive lines backward avoids misclassifying the 2013 bulk move, later package renames, or the 2022 descriptor refactor as the introducer. The trail ends at 1e6d4dfde55b188f81f7a862b9de541663abe7a2, where war-core/FileServer.java is added wholesale; its direct parent 840bf47c5fe108a702b6452b9bc586288317a2d5 has no such path, proving parent absence. This is a source-history SVN revision commit rather than a reconstructable squash, so there are no decomposed member SHAs. The code remains vulnerable at the 6.4.6 tag and is absent at 6.4.7 after direct fix caa6e6d1ac967ebd29b39e11c2ef5e7fd0047eec. Finally, inspection is restricted to the BIC object: it is a human SVN-era commit from 2009 with only a git-svn-id provenance trailer and no AI marker, so BIC-only attribution is NOT_AI.
